mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines by at least 0.25 percentage points over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate exceeding 4.0% indicates labor market slack that suppresses wage growth and corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals robust consumer demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where both HOUST > 1200 and RSAFS > 500000.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly industrial production growth rate exceeding 0.5% indicates robust manufacturing output, boosting corporate earnings expectations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO growth rate exceeds 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts over the prior 3 months reflects strengthening consumer demand for dwellings, correlating with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST increases by at least 0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Annual inflation exceeding 2.5% signals monetary policy tightening and reduced real equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strong employment growth (PAYEMS) and low unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a tight labor market supporting wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where PAYEMS growth rate exceeds 0.5% and UNRATE is below 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 2.5% indicates restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5%.
